title: MSRV 1.95 intrinsic feasibility for bipedal SIMD kernels
description:
## Context

CLAUDE.md §Breakdown-time feasibility check requires MSRV verification before SIMD-touching issues are dispatched. The previous `afac2262` incident cost a rework cycle when an AVX-512 ZMM-lane intrinsic turned out to be unstable on MSRV at the time. MSRV is now 1.95, but the verification must still happen.

This issue:

1. Identifies the AVX2 intrinsics needed for bipedal F₃ ops (lane-wise AND/XOR/OR over `__m256i`): `_mm256_and_si256`, `_mm256_xor_si256`, `_mm256_or_si256`, `_mm256_loadu_si256`, `_mm256_storeu_si256`. Confirms all are stable on MSRV 1.95.

2. Identifies the AVX-512 intrinsics needed for the [aspirational] AVX-512 path: `_mm512_and_si512`, `_mm512_xor_si512`, `_mm512_or_si512`, `_mm512_loadu_si512`, `_mm512_storeu_si512`. Confirms stability on MSRV 1.95 (or flags any unstable ones for #[cfg]-gating with scalar fallback).

3. Records `lscpu` output for the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X) confirming AVX2 yes, AVX-512 no — which makes AVX-512 paths `[aspirational]` from W3 onward.

4. Produces a tiny stub Cargo crate under `dev/research/intrinsic_feasibility_stub/` exercising both intrinsic sets and runs `rustup run 1.95.0 cargo check` to verify.

## Success Criteria

1. [hard] `dev/plans/d4_intrinsic_feasibility.md` lands and is attached via `jit doc add`, listing intended AVX2 and AVX-512 intrinsics with stability status on MSRV 1.95.
2. [hard] `rustup run 1.95.0 cargo check` succeeds on the stub crate for both AVX2 and AVX-512 code paths.
3. [hard] Doc records the dev host's `lscpu` AVX flags (already known: AVX2 yes, AVX-512 no) and confirms downstream W3 issues will gate AVX-512 as `[aspirational]`.
4. [hard] Doc references the prior `afac2262` lesson per CLAUDE.md.
